workflows.title: WF5 Plant floor change
workflows.description: Is an unticketed controller change an attack, is the process still safe, and how did they get there.
intro:
### Safety first
Do **not** isolate, reboot or push anything to a controller from the SOC. **Call the plant controls engineer on shift and the line supervisor before any action.** A controller in a bad state can hurt people. The SOC's job is to tell them what changed and from where.

**Use when:** Lead E, or WF3 Step 5 showed a controller event.  
**You need:** the plant and the asset.  
**Goal:** tell the plant team what changed, whether the process is safe, and who did it.

Work the steps in order. Each card says what to look at, what bad looks like and where to go next. Blue values in tables open the next workflow with that value filled in.

evidence.title: Unticketed changes at this plant (click an asset)
evidence.expr: sum by (ot_line, asset, event_type) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | site="$site" | change_ticket="" | event_type=~"program_download|controller_mode_change|write_request" [$__range]))

card.look: every unticketed controller change at this plant.
card.bad: more than one asset changed in a short window.
card.if_bad: click the asset to work it. Do the busiest one first.
card.if_clean: if the asset you were sent here for is not listed, its change had a ticket. Close the lead.

evidence.title: Asset event log
evidence.expr: {service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | site="$site" | asset="$asset" | line_format "{{.severity}}  {{.event_type}}  {{.description}}  [{{.technique_id}}]  ticket={{.change_ticket}}" | keep service_name

card.look: every event on the asset, oldest first.
card.bad: RUN to PROGRAM mode change, program download, then PROGRAM back to RUN, with no change ticket. That is someone replacing logic.
card.if_bad: phone the controls engineer now with the asset name and the time. Then Step 2.
card.if_clean: a ticketed change inside the window. Close the lead.

evidence.title: Setpoint writes
evidence.expr: {service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | site="$site" | asset="$asset" | event_type="write_request" | line_format "{{.description}}  by {{.user}} from {{.src_host}}" | keep service_name

card.bad: a setpoint pushed outside its engineering limits (oven, press force, torque, battery charge current).
card.if_bad: the controls engineer verifies the real value at the HMI and puts the line in a safe state. That is their call, not the SOC's.
card.if_clean: no setpoint writes. The logic change alone still needs review.

evidence.title: Source of the change (click the host)
evidence.expr: sum by (src_host, user, event_type) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | site="$site" | asset="$asset" [$__range]))

card.look: the workstation and account behind the change.
card.bad: an account that is not on the controls team, or an engineering workstation that also has EDR detections.
card.if_bad: click the host to open WF2 for it.
card.if_clean: the line's own engineer from their own workstation. Ask them whether they made the change.

steps.title: How did they reach the cell?

evidence.title: Connections into plant zones (click to open WF3)
evidence.expr: sum by (src_host, src_zone, dst_host, dst_zone, dst_port, rule) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-firewall"} | json | site="$site" | dst_zone=~"ot-.*" | action="allow" | src_host!~"HIST-.*" [$__range]))

card.look: who connected into the plant network zones at this site.
card.bad: a VPN address or office workstation going through the jump host, or anything into `ot-cell` that is not the historian.
card.if_bad: click the first host in the chain to open WF3 and walk it.
card.if_clean: only the historian and known engineering workstations.

evidence.title: New devices at this plant
evidence.expr: sum by (ot_line, asset, description) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | site="$site" | event_type="new_asset" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Controller-port scans inside cells
evidence.expr: count by (src_host) (sum by (src_host, dst_ip) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-firewall"} | json | site="$site" | src_zone="ot-cell" | action="deny" [$__range])))

card.look: new devices and scans inside the cells at this plant.
card.bad: an unknown device on a cell switch, or a workstation scanning controller ports (102 S7, 44818 EtherNet/IP, 502 Modbus).
card.if_bad: give the list to the controls engineer. Each one gets checked.
card.if_clean: no new devices and no scans.

decide.markdown:
### Decide
**Attack** if Step 1 shows an unticketed download or mode change **and** Step 3 or Step 4 is unexpected.

**Do these now (with the plant):**
1. Controls engineer restores the last known-good program and confirms setpoints.
2. Disable the account from Step 3 in the OT domain. Close the firewall rule from Step 4 that let the session in.
3. Preserve the controller project file and the workstation for forensics.

**Then go to:**
- WF2 for the workstation in Step 3 (click it)
- WF3 for the first host in Step 4 (click it)
- [[Case timeline for this asset]]

rule.close_if_false: Ticketed or explained change. Close the lead.
